source.publication: 2025 MI-1040 Forms and Instructions (includes Form 4884 instructions)
source.section: Schedule 1 line 25 (PDF page 17: Tier 2 Michigan Standard Deduction, 20,000 single, against all income types); Worksheet 2 lines 1-7a (PDF page 18); PDF pages 22-23 questions 1-6 (most beneficial of Worksheet 2 and Worksheet 3.3); MI-1040 lines 9a, 10, 13-17 (PDF page 10 Line 9a, Line 10, Line 17; PDF page 11 example: line 14 income subject to tax less line 15 exemptions = line 16 taxable income)

worked: Federal AGI = IRA distribution 5,000.00 + interest 14,000.00 + taxable Social Security 2,000.00 (gross 20,000.00; provisional income 29,000.00) = 21,000.00. Federal taxable income = 21,000.00 - federal standard deduction (15,750 + 1 x 2,000 age 65 or older = 17,750.00) = 3,250.00; given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored. Michigan (born 1950, past 67): Schedule 1 line 14 Social Security 2,000.00. Worksheet 2 line 1 20,000.00; lines 2, 4, 5 0.00; line 7 Tier 2 = 20,000.00, more than the 19,000.00 of income left (IRA 5,000.00 + interest 14,000.00), so it takes all of it: AGI 21,000.00 - 2,000.00 - 19,000.00 used = 0.00 (the form enters the whole worksheet amount, 20,000.00, on line 25, which would make line 14 21,000.00 - 2,000.00 - 20,000.00 = -1,000.00; taxable income is floored at 0 either way). Line 14 0.00; exemption 5,800.00; line 16 0.00. The other option, Worksheet 3.3, subtracts only the IRA 5,000.00: 21,000.00 - 2,000.00 - 5,000.00 - 5,800.00 = 8,200.00, tax 348.50; Tier 2 is more beneficial. Tax 0.00; state income tax 0.00.
